correctness.rationale: Graph distances are 2 inside a shore, 1 across nondeleted edges and 3 across deleted matched pairs, producing the displayed symmetric two-block D_p. The entire zero-sum subspace splits as H0=(1,-1), H+=(v,v), H-=(v,-v), with eigenvalues (n-1)2^p-n-3^p+1, 3^p-2^p-1 and 1-2^p-3^p and multiplicities 1,n-1,n-1. Their maximum determines the claimed exact gap. On 0<=p<=1, (2^p-1)/3^p strictly increases, so the root is unique IN (0,1) for n>=5; for p>1, 3^p>2^p+1 makes the H+ eigenvalue positive. The zero-sum Gram rank gives minimal snowflake dimension 3 for n=3,4, or 2n-2 for n>=5 at endpoint. Taylor expansion yields asymptotic improvement log(3)/((log2)^2(n-1)^2). Independent distance matrices and restricted numerical spectra matched n=3,4,5,6,8. Critical nuance: for n=5 the scalar equation has ANOTHER positive root above 1, but the RESULT/SLOGAN explicitly restrict uniqueness to (0,1), and p>1 is already ruled out by H+; no global root uniqueness is asserted.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a standard infinite graph family obtained by deleting the canonical perfect matching from K_nn. Their complete sharp p-negative-type classification, explicit ten-vertex first p=1 obstruction, normalized quantitative gap, exact least Euclidean snowflake ranks and strict matching-deletion comparison address natural embedding and metric invariants. The n cutoff is structurally forced by eigenvalue signs.
